title: Detect a same-path Engram binary upgrade and expose an explicit refresh path for running Engram MCP children
outcome: Relayed by Engram::Advisor (2026-09-05) from the Phoenix pilot: after an Engram upgrade, shell CLI calls (engram --version, next --json, doctor --json) report the new build fddd9bcac44a while the injected MCP child of a long-running session (Phoenix::Codex::Engram session-5867) returns next results without build_fingerprint/schema, i.e. an older binary still serving that session. TermAl compares the installed Engram descriptor by binary_path string only (session_crud.rs binary_path comparisons; EngramMcpInstalledDescriptor stores path + home), so an upgrade that overwrites the same path is invisible: the MCP child keeps running the old binary until the session runtime rotates for an unrelated reason, and no explicit refresh path exists. Desired: (1) record binary identity in the installed descriptor (file size+mtime or the engram build fingerprint from --version/doctor) and detect a mismatch against the configured binary; (2) surface staleness where the operator and the session can see it (Settings > Engram host status and the session wake/context note: "Engram MCP child runs build X, installed binary is build Y"); (3) an explicit refresh path - per session rotation at the next turn (runtime_reset_required) or a host-level "refresh Engram runtimes" action - never a silent restart of working sessions; refresh failures visible; (4) tests for detection, visibility and the refresh action. Acceptance: upgrading the engram binary in place is detected within one status refresh; affected sessions show the stale build and offer/receive the refresh; no session is restarted without an operator or session-initiated action; docs/features/engram-host-adapter.md describes the freshness contract.
